extracted.intended_audience: FDA and HHS policymakers, agency staff, and regulated industry (food, pharmacy, medical device) / small business stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of SBA Advocacy recommendations and stakeholder comments addressing deregulatory changes, compliance burdens, and recommended rule or guidance modifications across FDA-regulated sectors (pharmacy/OTC drugs, food labeling and safety, and medical devices). Intended as input for notice-and-comment rulemaking and agency reconsideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardize the ACNU self-assessment/proof process
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders recommend that the FDA standardize the ACNU process such that there is a common way for patients to prove that they fulfilled the ACNU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rule currently allows different manufacturers to establish varying methods for consumers to complete the self-assessment, which would require pharmacies to operationalize multiple sales processes and train salesclerks on different approaches, creating significant administrative burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek pharmacy input and standardize POS documentation for ACNU
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders ask CMS/FDA to standardize the ACNU self-assessment and to seek pharmacy input in the development of the systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rule would require costly POS modifications to enter 'stop' and to record proof that the patient provided the self-assessment and that the drug was appropriate, causing heightened administrative burden and hesitancy by pharmacies without clarity on manufacturers' approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage pharmacists / limit ACNU assessments to licensed pharmacies
rubrics_metrics.description: Pharmacy stakeholders believe ACNU availability should leverage pharmacist expertise by allowing only state licensed pharmacies to assist the patient with the necessary assessment processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making prescription and OTC medicines available may cause patient confusion and insurance changes; restricting assessments to pharmacists would use professional expertise to determine appropriateness and reduce confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdraw or reconsider Front-of-Package Nutrition Labeling (FOPL) proposed rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders (e.g., FMI) suggest the FDA should consider withdrawing the proposed FOPL rule requiring a 'Nutrition Info' box with percent Daily Value for sodium, saturated fat, and added sugars and interpretive markers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: rule would be burdensome and costly (label redesigns), benefits are not demonstrated given existing voluntary schemes (Facts Up Front), and FDA cost estimates are contested by industry; consider alternatives already in marketplace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reassess FOPL cost estimates and cost/benefit analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders argue the labeling costs assumed by the FDA are underestimated and provide industry estimates (e.g., $4,000-$8,000 per label) that exceed FDA's per-UPC estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocacy notes large disparities between FDA and industry cost estimates and recommends reevaluation before finalizing the rule; consider full impacts on small entities and reformulation likelihoods beyond FDA assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider statutory and First Amendment constraints on mandatory FOPL
rubrics_metrics.description: FMI believes the FOPL scheme raises statutory authority and First Amendment concerns because the FFDCA prescribes how nutrition labeling is mandated and does not authorize a mandatory selection of information separate from comprehensive nutrition information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA should evaluate legal authority before imposing a mandatory separate front-of-package disclosure regime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exempt certain alcohol beverages and kegged products from FOPL
rubrics_metrics.description: Brewers Association recommends exempting alcohol beverages (hard seltzers, hard ciders and other products under FDA jurisdiction) and kegged products from a final FOPL mandate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: split jurisdiction with TTB, small subset under FDA would face disproportionate costs and consumer confusion; kegged products analogous to restaurant sales and should be excluded; coordinate compliance dates with TTB labeling regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not certify 'no significant impact' under the RFA without reassessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocacy suggests that, given stakeholder cost estimates and alternatives, the FDA should not certify the final FOPL rule as having no significant impact on a substantial number of small entities under the RFA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continue outreach with affected stakeholders to identify and analyze significant alternatives that may lessen the rule’s costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update and assess voluntary sodium reduction goals before advancing
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders request FDA update Phase 1 sodium reduction targets using 2023 and 2024 product nutrition data and to assess the efficacy of Phase 1 targets before finalizing Phase 2 targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend using observed intake data (e.g., NHANES) to determine whether Phase 1 impacted consumption; account for reformulation timelines (18–36 months) and technological feasibility in certain categories before moving to Phase 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate 21 CFR §118.4(e) refrigeration requirement for surplus broiler hatching eggs
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders recommend exempting surplus broiler eggs from the shell egg refrigeration requirement that prevents their use for pasteurization and human food.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add an exemption to §118.1 for surplus broiler eggs when none are intended for human food without pasteurization; joint FSIS-FDA risk assessment indicates pasteurization can render these eggs safe, creating new revenue streams especially for small firms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide flexibility for traceability lot code tracking (FSMA Traceability Rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders recommend modifying the rule to allow retail stores and distribution centers to maintain a range of traceability lot codes included in a shipment, rather than the precise lot codes in a particular shipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves FDA's investigatory needs while reducing the operational and labor costs associated with case-level tracking across complex just-in-time distribution systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow algorithmic inference of traceability codes as an approved alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: Given advances in AI, stakeholders suggest FDA should allow food distributors to algorithmically infer traceability codes as an alternative to precise recording, provided algorithms are adequately evaluated and documented in FSMA traceability plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require evaluation/documentation of algorithms and include them in traceability plans to ensure reliability while reducing manual tracking burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exempt intracompany shipments from FSMA traceability requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders argue that intracompany shipments (e.g., central kitchens shipping to sister stores) should be exempt because internal recordkeeping suffices and external requirements impose heavy burdens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exempting such transfers would reduce excessive record volumes that threaten product availability (e.g., fresh-cut produce, deli salads) without clear public health benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot test traceability implementation before full enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders urge FDA to pilot or test the traceability regime before enforcement to assess real-world operability, particularly for lot-code requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot programs would expose practical implementation issues (e.g., invoices lacking lot codes, no practical manual logging) and reduce anxiety about readiness for enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amend definition of 'traceability lot code (TLC) source reference' to identify assigner rather than location
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders suggest allowing identification of the person or corporate entity responsible for assigning the TLC (e.g., GTIN) instead of requiring the specific location where the TLC was assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reduces burdens for processors operating across many locations while preserving FDA’s ability to conduct outbreak investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide flexibility/clarity to protect confidentiality of TLC source/reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppliers (notably seafood) are concerned about confidentiality of TLC source/reference (addresses, URLs, etc.) and request more flexibility or clarity on compliance while protecting commercial confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA should allow options or guidance that enable compliance without forcing disclosure of sensitive commercial information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborate with industry and FSIS; be transparent about interoperability findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders encourage FDA to collaborate with industry and USDA FSIS and to be transparent about findings on interoperability of systems within the food supply chain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joint work with FSIS and transparency will help evaluate problematic provisions and potential flexibilities during the 30-month extension period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate final rule revising 'healthy' nutrient content claim definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders suggest eliminating the final rule that revises when the term 'healthy' can be used, arguing it risks consumer confusion and duplicates/inconsistently overlaps with other FDA rules (FOPL, sodium guidelines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid imposing new 'healthy' standard that conflicts with existing frameworks and creates additional labeling costs without clear public health benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revoke or modernize 21 CFR Part 11 electronic recordkeeping requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Food and device stakeholders recommend revoking the Part 11 rules requiring system validation, audit trails, data integrity controls, and electronic signature security as outdated, unworkable, and restrictive of innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA previously exercised enforcement discretion; stakeholders argue the regulation should be removed or modernized because electronic systems are now commonplace and the requirements impose unnecessary burdens, especially on small facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revoke warning statement requirement for high-protein products (21 CFR 101.17(d)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders recommend revoking the regulation that requires foods deriving >50% of calories from protein and represented for weight reduction to bear a warning that the product should be used only as a food supplement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule is seen as outdated and unnecessary given current dietary practices and guidelines; compliance costs are not justified by commensurate public health benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize permitting salt substitutes in standards of identity (SOI)
rubrics_metrics.description: FMI requests FDA finalize the proposed rule to amend SOI regulations that specify salt as required or optional ingredient to permit use of salt substitutes in standardized foods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a horizontal approach to modernize standards of identity addressing use of salt, which would promote innovation, reduce sodium, and be efficient across rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide regulatory relief and flexibilities for very small farms under FSMA
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders report FSMA burdens (produce safety rule) impose high compliance costs on very small farms, complex eligibility rules for Tester-Hagan exemptions, excessive water testing requirements, and overwhelm small producers with deadlines and compliance complexity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA should revise rules to provide relief for very small farms, simplify exemption eligibility determination, revisit water testing burdens (Microbial Water Quality Profiles), and offer outreach and alternatives to lessen financial/time costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide cost relief or discounts for FDA Medical Device Establishment registration fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Small medical device manufacturers request cost relief from registration fees which are the same for small entities as large firms and increase substantially each year (example: $9,280).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend exemptions or deep discounts for small entities and potential exemption for simple Class I devices sold directly to the public; note lack of small-entity discounts compared to other fees (e.g., patents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use CURES Act Section 3054 authority to exempt low-risk devices from 510(k)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders urge FDA to use CURES Act authority to identify Class I/II devices that no longer warrant 510(k) review and exempt them, per statutory requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applying these exemptions provides risk-based regulatory relief, conserves agency resources, and supports innovation for patients and small manufacturers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use FDARA Section 707 accessory classification authority to classify accessories as Class I and publish list regularly
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders encourage FDA to meet its statutory requirement to publish a new list of accessories suitable for distinct Class I classification at least once every 5 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinct classification will provide certainty and reduce burdens for small accessory manufacturers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescind premarket notification requirements for point-of-care (POC) in vitro tests in specific CFR sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders recommend rescinding regulations that require premarket notification for in vitro devices intended for POC testing across many device regulation sections (e.g., 21 CFR §§ 862.9, 864.9, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POC tests are often low-risk and valuable for public health (e.g., COVID-19); categorical limitations based on intended 'POC' setting create unnecessary hurdles and impede deployment and innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescind Part 11 requirements as applied to medical device stakeholders (validation, audit trails, record retention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Device representatives recommend rescinding Part 11 regulations requiring validation, audit trails, record retention, and electronic record copying that date to 2003 and are now outdated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA previously used enforcement discretion; stakeholders emphasize the substantial resource expenditures and argue the rule should be removed or modernized to reflect current practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescind 'Best Practices for Selecting a Predicate Device' draft guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders recommend rescinding the draft guidance that recommends characteristics for selecting a predicate device and disclosure of predicate selection processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No statutory basis exists to enforce such recommendations; disclosure could force proprietary information and is irrelevant to substantial equivalence determinations under 21 CFR § 807.92.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescind 'Evidentiary Expectations for 510(k) Implant Devices' draft guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders request rescission of this draft guidance which appears to change the definition of an implanted device and includes blanket recommendations not considering device risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance is inconsistent with FDA's benefit-risk and 'least burdensome' principles and may impose undue requirements beyond statutory standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescind 'Use of Clinical Data in Premarket Notification 510(k) Submissions' draft guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders argue this draft guidance includes examples/recommendations that shift expectations towards a PMA-like safety and effectiveness standard rather than the statutory substantial equivalence standard for 510(k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidance could impose undue burdens; it should be eliminated to preserve statutory standards for 510(k) submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescind 'Evaluation of Thermal Effects of Medical Devices' draft guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Small medical device stakeholders recommend rescinding this draft guidance as overly broad, applying to many device types and all premarket submissions and potentially impeding development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance conflicts with existing FDA policies and standards, lacks a risk-based approach, could delay marketing of beneficial products, and contradicts the least burdensome principle; FDA should withdraw and instead develop tailored, standards-based approaches in consultation with industry.
